findings.reason: a worker repairs the guard condition at the caller, which is in the write paths; the mislabel costs navigation, not scope.
findings.text: §5 calls `_require_write_paths_in_authority` "the fence (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` near line 911)", but line 911 is the call site inside `plan_dispatch`; the fence itself is defined in `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1983`, and §1 of the same plan names that file correctly, so the section contradicts its own sibling

findings.reason: the section's repair premise points at a guard both paths already run, so a worker reaching the fallback delivers only a regression test and §1's fourth case is left unexplained; the section must name the real divergence (the dry run stops at `plan_dispatch` while the launch continues into `dispatch`'s own checks) or be re-scoped to the regression guard.
findings.text: §5 says "the worker first reproduces §1's fourth case: a `--dry-run` whose write path resolves under `~/.cache` answers ok while the same dispatch without `--dry-run` is refused", and offers the causes as "`repo` unresolved, `verdict.ok` false, or another"; but the dry-run branch calls `plan_dispatch(..., repo=repo, ...)` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py` near line 1923) and the fence at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:911` sits inside `if verdict.ok and repo is not None`, so `repo` is not None on the dry-run path and a dry run that answers ok had `verdict.ok` true — both named conditions are ruled out by the section's own citation, and the case cannot reproduce at the fence it blames

findings.reason: the done-when's fifth case asserts the value is "stored with it in `dispatch_options`", and a worker must invent the parameter (or smuggle a dynamic attribute onto `TaskNode`, which the section forbids by name) before the case can pass; naming the channel in the deliverable removes that decision from the worker.
findings.text: §3 says "A batch entry gains `plan_link` and `unplanned_reason` fields (`BATCH_ENTRY_FIELDS`), which `queue_requests` records in the same `dispatch_options`" while requiring "no new `TaskNode` field"; but `queue_requests` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:293`) takes only `TaskNode` objects and builds `dispatch_options` from its own parameters and constants (`dispatch.py` near line 354, hardcoded to `project`, `session`, `no_watch`), and `_queue_batch` passes nothing but `[node]` plus lane/config (`reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py` near line 573), so no described channel carries the entry's value to the entry's pointer

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §5 attributes `_require_write_paths_in_authority` to `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` near line 911, which is its call site; the function is defined in `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1983`. Every other anchor the three units name resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2 declares five negative controls, one per shared refusal; §3 three; §5 one, with a stated substitute control when its reproduction does not fire. Every case names a concrete test file and a base-revision failure delta.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is placed "under the run directory", a durable path outside any session scratchpad, and each is required to open with its revision and literal command and close with `EXIT=`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames describe behaviour (`test_every_path_meets_the_node_contract.py`, `test_a_brief_run_names_its_plan_at_dispatch.py`, `test_a_dry_run_fences_write_paths.py`), and no plan label, ticket number or version tag appears in them or in the symbols the units cite.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §5's premise is refuted by the code it cites (the dry run passes `repo` and reaches the fence), and §3 states that `queue_requests` records a batch entry's plan link while forbidding the only field that could carry it to that function.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one whole-node judge on every path, §3 one plan-link record kept at dispatch, §5 one fence applied by the dry run; no node carries two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares `plan-after` `a-dry-run-must-resolve-what-the-real-call-resolves` (whose §5 the snapshot records as `done`), and `plan-section-depends-on` wires `s3` and `s5` to `a-refusal-comes-before-the-work#s2`, which matches the file-sharing the followup names.
